name: Wrath (ira) as capital vice
plainSummary: In this list, wrath denotes unjust anger—desire for vengeance or cruelty out of proportion to a real or perceived wrong.
description: Derived principle: ira (wrath or anger as vice) is the capital vice of disordered anger—resentment, rage, or cruelty that seeks harm beyond just defense or proportionate correction; classically distinguished from righteous anger at genuine injustice.
foundationStrengthRationale: Anger's moral status is debated everywhere; tradition's distinction between ordered and disordered anger remains useful but not universally accepted.

pros.claim: Tracks cycles of retaliation and dehumanization familiar in criminal and political life.
pros.evidence: Restorative justice and conflict theory both study how unchecked anger entrenches harm.

cons.claim: Anger is sometimes a fitting response to oppression; labeling it wrath can silence legitimate outrage.
cons.evidence: Liberation ethics and social movements debate when anger is prophetic versus destructive.
